title: 了 (le) in Chinese: HSK 1 Grammar with Examples
description: How to use 了 (le) in Chinese: 了 after the verb for finished actions, 了 at the end for a change, negatives with 没有, questions, and HSK 1 examples.
h1: How to Use 了 (le) in Chinese
lede: 了 (le) is a small word with two main jobs. After a verb, it shows that an action is finished. At the end of a sentence, it shows that something has changed or is new. It is one of the first grammar points of HSK 1.

sections.h2: 了 after the verb: a finished action
paras: Put 了 straight after the verb to say the action happened and is complete. This works best when the object has a number or a describing word in front of it, such as 三本书 or 很多东西. A short object on its own, as in 我买了书, often sounds unfinished, as if more is coming.

examples.py: Wǒ mǎi le sān běn shū.
Tā mǎi le hěn duō dōngxi.
Wǒmen kàn le yí ge diànyǐng.

sections.h2: 了 at the end: something has changed
paras: When 了 comes at the end of the sentence, it tells the listener that the situation is new: it has started raining, it is now eight o'clock, you have changed your plans. This 了 can also follow an adjective, as in 天冷了, or a negative with 不, as in 我不想去了.
With a simple verb and object, such as 吃饭 or 睡觉, putting 了 at the end is the natural way to say it has happened.

examples.py: Bā diǎn le, wǒmen qù xuéxiào ba.
examples.en: It's eight o'clock, let's go to school.
I don't want to go any more.

sections.h2: Two 了 together: up to now
paras: With a length of time, you can use 了 in both places. The action began in the past and is still going on now.

examples.py: Wǒ xué le yì nián Zhōngwén le.
examples.en: I've been learning Chinese for a year.

examples.py: Wǒ zài zhèr zhù le sān nián le.
examples.en: I've lived here for three years.

paras: To say an action did not happen, use 没有 before the verb and drop 了. A very common mistake is to keep 了 and say 他没有来了 instead of 他没有来. Use 还没有 for "not yet".
To ask whether something has happened, add 吗 after 了, or end the question with 了没有. Answer yes with the verb and 了, or no with 还没有.

sections.h2: 了 is not a past tense
paras: Learners often add 了 to everything that happened in the past. Chinese does not need it there. If you are describing how things were, or something you did regularly, a time word such as 昨天 or 去年 is enough.

examples.en: Last year I worked in China.

worksheet.title: 了 (le) Worksheet: HSK 1 Printable with Answers
worksheet.description: A free printable 了 (le) worksheet for HSK 1: 20 exercises (了 or 没有, word order, fix the mistake) with an answer key.

exercises.instructions: Write 了 or 没有 in each gap. The English tells you what the sentence means.

items.en: I drank a lot of water.
I don't want to eat any more.

exercises.instructions: Write the words as one correct sentence.

items.en: He ate a lot of rice.
He's been working here for two years.
answers: 他在这儿工作了两年了。

exercises.instructions: Each sentence has one mistake. Write the correct sentence.

items.en: I was very busy last year.
